Validate or Coerce Positive Integer Values

Source: R/05_tools.R
positive_integer.Rd

Utilities for validating and coercing positive integer-valued numeric vectors.

is_positive_integer() tests whether every element of m is finite, integer-valued, greater than or equal to one, and representable as a base R integer.

as_positive_integer() performs the same validation and converts m to an integer vector. It raises an error when validation fails.

Usage

is_positive_integer(m)

as_positive_integer(m)

Arguments

m

An object to validate or coerce.

Value

is_positive_integer() returns a single logical value.

as_positive_integer() returns m as an integer vector, or raises an error if m is not a valid positive integer vector.

Details

A value is considered a positive integer when it:

  • is numeric;

  • has positive length;

  • contains no missing or infinite values;

  • contains only whole numbers;

  • is greater than or equal to one; and

  • does not exceed .Machine$integer.max.

Zero, negative numbers, fractional values, NA, NaN, Inf, and non-numeric objects are rejected.

Examples

is_positive_integer(3)
#> [1] TRUE
is_positive_integer(c(1, 2, 3))
#> [1] TRUE
is_positive_integer(c(1, 2.5))
#> [1] FALSE
is_positive_integer(0)
#> [1] FALSE

as_positive_integer(3)
#> [1] 3
as_positive_integer(c(1, 2, 3))
#> [1] 1 2 3
